definitionEn: a lack of something that is needed.
existingExample: Vitamin D deficiency is common in winter.

definitionEn: drinking a large amount of alcohol in a short time.
existingExample: Binge drinking is a serious problem among some students.

definitionEn: a device that records steps and heart rate.
meaningVi: thiết bị theo dõi vận động
existingExample: Fitness trackers motivate some people to walk more.

definitionEn: the health of the population as a whole.
existingExample: Public health campaigns have reduced smoking rates.

definitionEn: careful about health.
existingExample: Health-conscious consumers are buying more plant-based food.

definitionEn: made from or consisting of plants rather than animal products.
existingExample: A plant-based diet can lower cholesterol.

definitionEn: a fatty substance in the blood.
existingExample: High cholesterol increases the risk of heart attacks.

definitionEn: breathing in other people's cigarette smoke.
existingExample: Passive smoking is particularly harmful to children.

definitionEn: a tax on products containing a lot of sugar.
existingExample: A sugar tax encouraged manufacturers to reduce sugar in drinks.

definitionEn: a government that interferes too much in people's personal choices.
meaningVi: nhà nước bảo mẫu (can thiệp quá mức)
existingExample: Critics called the sugar tax an example of the nanny state.

definitionEn: individuals being responsible for their own choices.
existingExample: Some argue that health is largely a matter of personal responsibility.

definitionEn: providing medical care remotely by video or phone.
existingExample: Telemedicine allows rural patients to consult specialists.

definitionEn: workers in direct contact with the public, such as nurses.
existingExample: Frontline workers faced enormous pressure during the pandemic.

definitionEn: the number of deaths in a group over a period.
existingExample: Infant mortality rates have fallen sharply worldwide.

definitionEn: the study of how diseases spread in populations.
existingExample: Epidemiology helps governments predict outbreaks.

definitionEn: an illness that could be avoided through vaccination or lifestyle.
existingExample: Millions of children still die from preventable diseases.

definitionEn: changes in health resulting from care or circumstances.
existingExample: Poverty is linked to poorer health outcomes.

definitionEn: activities involving sitting for long periods.
existingExample: Standing desks can reduce sedentary behaviour at work.

definitionEn: to use up energy through physical activity.
existingExample: Regular brisk walking and cycling help people burn calories more effectively than relying on dietary restriction alone.

definitionEn: dried leaves smoked in cigarettes.
existingExample: Many countries have banned tobacco advertising.

definitionEn: a patient who visits hospital without staying overnight.
existingExample: Minor surgery is often done on an outpatient basis.

definitionEn: the number of new cases of a disease in a population over a period.
existingExample: The incidence of diabetes has risen in many developing countries.

definitionEn: a statistical link between two things that does not prove one causes the other.
existingExample: Studies show an association between poor sleep and weight gain.

definitionEn: not agreeing with each other; changing in a way that is not reliable.
existingExample: Earlier studies produced inconsistent results.

definitionEn: to hide something so that it cannot be seen or noticed.
existingExample: Average figures can mask large differences between regions.

definitionEn: a smaller group taken from a larger group.
existingExample: A subset of participants was asked to keep a food diary.

definitionEn: to consider a factor when analysing something; to form a particular amount of.
existingExample: Statistical models must account for confounding variables such as age, income, and lifestyle.

definitionEn: a relationship in which one thing directly makes another happen.
existingExample: Observational studies cannot prove cause and effect.

definitionEn: to be careful when making judgements or decisions.
existingExample: Readers should exercise caution when interpreting headlines about diet.

definitionEn: to record or measure something accurately.
existingExample: A single survey cannot capture the complexity of people's diets.

definitionEn: made by putting processed ingredients back together into a new form.
meaningVi: được tái chế biến, hoàn nguyên
existingExample: Some cheap sausages contain reconstituted meat.

definitionEn: The condition of suffering from a disease or the rate of illness within a defined population.
meaningVi: tỷ lệ mắc bệnh hoặc gánh nặng bệnh tật trong cộng đồng
existingExample: Improving urban air quality substantially lowers respiratory morbidity among both primary schoolchildren and elderly residents.

definitionEn: The simultaneous presence of two or more chronic medical conditions in the same patient.
existingExample: Hospital planners must account for rising comorbidity as ageing populations increasingly manage diabetes alongside heart disease.

definitionEn: The medical investigation or set of biological and environmental causes underlying a specific disease.
meaningVi: căn nguyên học, tập hợp nguyên nhân gây ra bệnh lý
existingExample: Uncovering the multifactorial aetiology of autoimmune disorders has shifted clinical research toward gut and environmental triggers.

definitionEn: A biological agent such as a bacterium, virus, or fungus capable of causing infectious disease in a host.
meaningVi: tác nhân vi sinh gây bệnh (virus, vi khuẩn, ký sinh trùng)
existingExample: Rapid genomic sequencing allows public laboratories to identify an emerging airborne pathogen within days of detection.

definitionEn: Medical treatment or preventive intervention administered proactively to stop a disease from developing or spreading.
meaningVi: biện pháp dự phòng y khoa nhằm ngăn chặn bệnh khởi phát
existingExample: Targeted dental prophylaxis in public schools has dramatically cut childhood cavity rates at a fraction of surgical costs.

definitionEn: Specialised medical and emotional support focused on relieving pain and distress in patients with serious or incurable illnesses.
meaningVi: chăm sóc giảm nhẹ nhằm nâng cao chất lượng sống
existingExample: Expanding home-based palliative care enables terminally ill patients to preserve dignity and comfort surrounded by family.

definitionEn: The rapid clinical assessment of patients to determine the urgency of treatment when healthcare resources are stretched.
meaningVi: sàng lọc và phân loại mức độ ưu tiên cấp cứu
existingExample: Well-trained nursing staff oversee emergency-room triage so life-threatening cardiac cases receive immediate intervention.

definitionEn: A clinician's informed forecast of the likely course, duration, and outcome of a medical condition.
meaningVi: tiên lượng y khoa về diễn tiến và khả năng hồi phục
existingExample: Routine national screening programmes have transformed the long-term prognosis for several formerly fatal cancers.

definitionEn: A temporary or permanent reduction or disappearance of the signs and symptoms of a serious disease.
existingExample: Breakthrough targeted therapies have enabled thousands of leukaemia patients to achieve sustained clinical remission.

definitionEn: The gradual period of rest and biological recuperation following serious illness, injury, or major surgery.
meaningVi: giai đoạn dưỡng bệnh và phục hồi thể lực sau phẫu thuật
existingExample: Statutory paid sick leave ensures working-class patients can complete proper convalescence instead of returning prematurely to strain.

definitionEn: Carrying a disease or infection while showing no noticeable physical signs or clinical symptoms.
meaningVi: không có triệu chứng dù đã mang mầm bệnh
existingExample: Widespread asymptomatic transmission complicates outbreak containment because infected travellers remain unaware they are contagious.

definitionEn: Relating to infectious diseases that jump from vertebrate animals to human populations.
meaningVi: lây truyền tự nhiên từ động vật sang con người
existingExample: Encroachment into tropical wildlife habitats elevates contact with wild reservoirs and heightens zoonotic spillover risks.

definitionEn: Unintentionally induced in a patient as an adverse consequence of medical examination, medication, or surgical intervention.
meaningVi: phát sinh ngoài ý muốn do quá trình điều trị y khoa
existingExample: Electronic prescribing audits have sharply curtailed iatrogenic drug interactions in overburdened regional clinics.

definitionEn: Originating or acquired inside a hospital or clinical care facility during medical admission.
existingExample: Rigorous ward ventilation and strict hand-hygiene protocols are essential for curbing drug-resistant nosocomial infections.

definitionEn: Involving physical illness or bodily symptoms significantly caused or aggravated by mental stress or emotional factors.
existingExample: Primary-care physicians increasingly recognise how chronic workplace anxiety manifests through debilitating psychosomatic migraines.

definitionEn: The internal twenty-four-hour biological clock regulating sleep-wake cycles, hormone secretion, and metabolic processes.
meaningVi: nhịp sinh học ngày đêm điều phối giấc ngủ và nội tiết
existingExample: Prolonged nocturnal blue-light exposure disrupts the human circadian rhythm and elevates long-term cardiometabolic risk.

definitionEn: The complex ecological community of trillions of beneficial microorganisms inhabiting the human digestive tract and skin.
meaningVi: hệ vi sinh vật cộng sinh trong đường ruột và cơ thể
existingExample: Nutritional scientists increasingly link a diverse fibre-rich diet to a resilient gut microbiome that bolsters immune regulation.

definitionEn: The study of how environmental exposures and lifestyle choices alter gene activity without changing the underlying DNA sequence.
existingExample: Findings from epigenetics suggest that early-childhood nutrition and maternal stress leave lasting biochemical marks on adult health.

definitionEn: A measurable biological molecule, cellular trait, or physiological indicator used to detect disease or track treatment response.
meaningVi: dấu ấn sinh học chỉ thị tình trạng sức khỏe/bệnh lý
existingExample: Identifying a reliable blood biomarker for early Alzheimer's could allow clinicians to intervene years before memory loss begins.

definitionEn: A medical model that customises disease prevention and treatment to an individual's genetic profile, environment, and lifestyle.
meaningVi: y học chính xác cá thể hóa theo đặc điểm gen
existingExample: Oncologists harness precision medicine to match tumour mutations with targeted drugs, sparing patients ineffective chemotherapy.

definitionEn: Medical treatment that stimulates, restores, or redirects the body's own immune defences to combat cancer or allergies.
meaningVi: liệu pháp miễn dịch chống ung thư và bệnh lý
existingExample: Modern checkpoint-inhibitor immunotherapy has extended survival rates for advanced melanoma patients who previously had few options.

definitionEn: The ongoing scientific monitoring, detection, and prevention of adverse drug reactions after medicines enter clinical markets.
existingExample: Strong national pharmacovigilance registries ensure rare pharmaceutical side effects are flagged swiftly and transparent warnings issued.

definitionEn: Coordinated clinical initiatives to optimise antibiotic prescribing so therapeutic effectiveness is preserved and resistance minimised.
meaningVi: quản lý sử dụng kháng sinh hợp lý và có trách nhiệm
existingExample: Hospitals implementing strict antimicrobial stewardship have reduced unnecessary broad-spectrum prescriptions without harming patient recovery.

definitionEn: Delay in acceptance or refusal of recommended immunisations despite the availability of safe, accessible vaccination services.
meaningVi: tâm lý chần chừ hoặc từ chối tiêm chủng vắc-xin
existingExample: Combating vaccine hesitancy demands empathetic dialogue with trusted community doctors rather than dismissive government mandates.

definitionEn: An individual's capacity to obtain, comprehend, and act upon reliable medical guidance to make sound health decisions.
existingExample: Low health literacy frequently leads elderly patients to misread dosage schedules, driving preventable emergency hospital readmissions.

definitionEn: Industrially formulated edible products made mostly from refined extracts, additives, and flavour enhancers with minimal whole ingredients.
meaningVi: thực phẩm siêu chế biến công nghiệp giàu phụ gia
existingExample: Longitudinal cohort studies associate high daily intake of ultra-processed food with elevated risks of obesity and depression.

definitionEn: A numerical ranking indicating how rapidly a carbohydrate-containing food raises blood glucose levels after consumption.
meaningVi: chỉ số đường huyết đo tốc độ tăng đường máu
existingExample: Dietitians recommend choosing legumes and whole oats with a low glycaemic index to maintain steady daytime energy levels.

definitionEn: A cluster of co-occurring physiological risk factors—including abdominal obesity, raised blood pressure, and insulin resistance.
meaningVi: hội chứng rối loạn chuyển hóa làm tăng nguy cơ tim mạch
existingExample: Regular brisk walking and modest dietary fibre increases can reverse early metabolic syndrome before permanent arterial damage occurs.

definitionEn: Characterised by the progressive structural breakdown and death of nerve cells in the brain or spinal cord.
meaningVi: thoái hóa thần kinh tiến triển làm suy giảm tế bào
existingExample: Rising global life expectancy has made funding therapies for neurodegenerative illnesses an urgent fiscal and humanitarian priority.

definitionEn: A gradual deterioration in memory, reasoning speed, attention, or executive mental abilities, often linked to ageing.
meaningVi: sự suy giảm dần chức năng nhận thức và trí nhớ
existingExample: Sustained social engagement, bilingualism, and cardiovascular fitness are consistently associated with slower age-related cognitive decline.

definitionEn: Relating to medical care, clinical services, and health conditions specifically affecting older adults.
existingExample: Rapidly ageing East Asian societies face acute shortages of trained geriatric specialists and community rehabilitation nurses.

definitionEn: Relating to the specialised branch of medicine dedicated to infants, children, and adolescents.
existingExample: Expanding rural paediatric clinics ensures developmental delays are identified and treated during the most responsive early years.

definitionEn: The systematic, continuous collection and analysis of population health data to detect outbreaks early and guide interventions.
meaningVi: hệ thống giám sát dịch tễ học nhằm phát hiện sớm dịch
existingExample: Wastewater testing has become an economical pillar of epidemiological surveillance for tracking seasonal respiratory surges.

definitionEn: Making a person physically or mentally extremely weak and severely impairing daily functioning.
existingExample: Untreated chronic lower-back pain remains one of the most debilitating causes of lost productivity among working adults.

definitionEn: To process nutrients, toxins, or pharmaceutical compounds chemically inside living cells to produce energy or eliminate waste.
meaningVi: chuyển hóa chất dinh dưỡng hoặc dược chất trong cơ thể
existingExample: Genetic variations explain why different patients metabolise the exact same prescribed dose of blood thinners at markedly different speeds.

definitionEn: To confer protective immunity against an infectious disease by administering a safe vaccine.
meaningVi: tạo miễn dịch phòng bệnh qua tiêm chủng vắc-xin
existingExample: Mobile rural clinics have enabled public health ministries to immunise millions of remote infants against measles and polio.

definitionEn: To introduce an antigenic agent into a person or animal to stimulate protective antibodies against a targeted pathogen.
meaningVi: chủng ngừa bằng cách đưa kháng nguyên an toàn vào cơ thể
existingExample: Coordinated international funding made it possible to inoculate vulnerable healthcare staff swiftly during the winter flu peak.

definitionEn: the percentage of people who want to work but have no job.
existingExample: The unemployment rate among young graduates has risen sharply.

definitionEn: the likelihood that you will keep your job.
existingExample: Many young people value job security more than a high salary.

definitionEn: the balance between time spent working and time for your personal life.
meaningVi: cân bằng công việc và cuộc sống
existingExample: Flexible hours help employees achieve a better work-life balance.

definitionEn: money paid for work or a service.
existingExample: Nurses argue that their remuneration does not reflect their responsibilities.

definitionEn: the rate at which a worker or company produces goods or results.
existingExample: Some trials suggest that a four-day week can boost productivity.

definitionEn: a period when the economy of a country is doing badly.
existingExample: Many small businesses closed during the recession.

definitionEn: a person who starts a business and takes financial risks.
existingExample: Governments can support young entrepreneurs with low-interest loans.

definitionEn: a general increase in prices.
existingExample: Rising inflation has reduced the purchasing power of ordinary families.

definitionEn: the belief that buying more and more goods is good.
existingExample: Rampant consumerism encourages people to buy things they do not need.

definitionEn: a labour market made up of short-term, freelance jobs.
meaningVi: nền kinh tế việc làm tự do
existingExample: Workers in the gig economy often lack sick pay and pensions.

definitionEn: the unequal distribution of income between people in a society.
existingExample: Progressive taxation is one way to reduce income inequality.

definitionEn: workers who have special training or experience.
existingExample: There is a severe shortage of skilled workers in the construction industry.

definitionEn: the feeling of pleasure you get from doing your job.
meaningVi: sự hài lòng với công việc
existingExample: Recognition from managers is a key factor in job satisfaction.

definitionEn: your chances of success in your future career.
existingExample: Speaking a second language can significantly improve your career prospects.

definitionEn: losing your job because your employer no longer needs you.
meaningVi: sự mất việc do cắt giảm
existingExample: Thousands of workers faced redundancy when the factory closed.

definitionEn: something that encourages you to do something.
existingExample: Tax incentives could encourage companies to hire older workers.

definitionEn: to pay another company to do work instead of doing it yourself.
existingExample: Many firms outsource customer service to reduce costs.

definitionEn: the lowest pay that employers are legally allowed to pay.
existingExample: Raising the minimum wage can lift families out of poverty.

definitionEn: all the people who work in a company, industry or country.
existingExample: A well-educated workforce attracts foreign investment.

definitionEn: an increase in the amount of goods and services a country produces.
existingExample: Tourism has been a major driver of economic growth in the region.

definitionEn: producing a lot of money.
existingExample: Software engineering has become one of the most lucrative careers.

definitionEn: extreme tiredness caused by working too hard for too long.
existingExample: Long working hours without breaks often lead to burnout.

definitionEn: an arrangement that lets employees choose their hours or place of work.
existingExample: Offering flexible working helps companies keep talented parents.

definitionEn: the state of being very poor.
existingExample: Access to education is one of the most effective ways to lift people out of poverty.

definitionEn: a large company that operates in several countries.
existingExample: Multinational corporations can bring jobs but may also harm local businesses.

definitionEn: the supply of and demand for workers.
existingExample: Graduates face an increasingly competitive labour market.

definitionEn: relating to manual or industrial work.
existingExample: Blue-collar workers were hit hardest by factory closures.

definitionEn: unskilled and of low status.
existingExample: Many migrants take menial jobs despite holding degrees.

definitionEn: a job that is available.
existingExample: The company has several vacancies for engineers.

definitionEn: to find new people to work for an organisation.
existingExample: Hospitals struggle to recruit experienced nurses.

definitionEn: to find and persuade someone to leave their job for another.
existingExample: She was headhunted by a rival bank.

definitionEn: changing jobs frequently.
existingExample: Job-hopping is common among young professionals.
